assumptions.choice: The spec's literal Fibonacci/price levels (low 74,500, high 124,000, retracement ~94,000) belong to a different, non-AAPL instrument and cannot be applied to AAPL OHLCV (~$50-$260 over the feed period); the specified method (0.618 retracement of the last significant upward swing) was generalized to compute levels dynamically from AAPL's own detected swing lows/highs instead of the hardcoded numbers.
assumptions.reason: The feed is fixed as AAPL daily bars; hardcoding the given price levels would never trigger and would misrepresent the strategy's intent, so the retracement mechanism was preserved and the absolute prices were made data-relative.

assumptions.choice: Defined a local low/high as a 5-bar fractal (2 bars on each side), confirmed with a 2-bar lag.
assumptions.reason: The spec says the trendline is 'built from local lows' but does not define the swing-detection window.

assumptions.choice: Support trendline is the straight line through the two most recently confirmed ascending swing lows, extrapolated to the current bar; recalculated whenever a new swing low forms.
assumptions.reason: The spec names an uptrend trendline from local lows but not the number of points or fitting method; two-point construction matches manual chart trendline drawing.

assumptions.choice: The 'last significant upward move' used for the Fibonacci leg is the most recent confirmed swing-low-to-later-swing-high pair whose gain is at least 3%.
assumptions.reason: The spec gives no numeric significance threshold; 3% is a reasonable noise filter for daily AAPL swings.

assumptions.choice: Used SMA(50) as the optional trend filter, with 'pointing upward' defined as sma[0] > sma[-1] versus the prior bar.
assumptions.reason: Spec offers 'SMA 50 or 200' without choosing one; 50 was picked as the more responsive of the two named options.

assumptions.choice: Implemented only the quantified 2:1 reward:risk take-profit (entry + 2 x (entry - stop)); the alternative 'next significant resistance level' rule was not implemented.
assumptions.reason: The spec offers the two as alternatives ('or'), and 'next significant resistance' has no defined detection method in the spec, so implementing it would require inventing an undeclared indicator.

assumptions.choice: Stop-loss placed at the lower (more conservative) of the current trendline value and the most recent confirmed swing low, minus a 0.1% buffer.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'slightly below the broken support trendline or below the nearest local low' without specifying how to combine the two or how large 'slightly' is.

assumptions.choice: Risk per trade fixed at 1% (the low end of the stated 1-2% range) of current broker equity; size = (equity x 1%) / (estimated entry - stop), with entry estimated from the signal bar's close.
assumptions.reason: Spec gives a 1-2% range without a fixed value; 1% was chosen as the more conservative bound, matching the spec's own 1%/2% risk:reward illustration. Actual fill occurs at the next bar's open per backtrader defaults, so realized risk may deviate slightly from the 1% target.

assumptions.choice: Stop-loss and take-profit are submitted as real OCO Stop/Limit orders once entry fills (one cancels the other on execution); the opposite trendline break is checked each bar and closes the position at market. A pending fib-touch entry setup is invalidated after a single touch (whether or not it results in a fill) or by an opposing trendline break, with no separate expiry timer.
assumptions.reason: Spec does not specify order types for SL/TP or an expiration window for the pullback setup awaiting the 0.618 touch; real bracket-style orders give price-accurate fills and OCO behavior matches standard risk-management practice.
